body: Forward test of the flags-judgment context method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.65 (naive base rate 0.55) that: Optimum Communications (ex-Altice USA) or its subsidiary CSC Holdings files for Chapter 11 by 30-Jun-2027. Evidence: 8-K (16-Nov-2026): CSC Holdings 'elected not to make' ~$102.5m of interest due 16-Nov-2026 on its 11.25% 2028, 4.5% 2031 guaranteed and 5% 2031 notes, entering a 30-day grace period; negotiating with 'the steering committee of an ad hoc group of debtholders' that 'holds the vast majority of the nearly $22 billion of debt'; any deal 'would result in a material reduction of the indebtedness'; 'cannot provide any assurances that such an agreement will be reached within the Grace Period or at all'; cash $1.1bn at 30-Sep-2026. 10-Q (Q2 2026, as restated): going-concern 'substantial doubt' with $4.1225bn principal maturing April 2027 and $2.225bn later in 2027 vs cash $1.30bn; Q2 2026 financials restated for an ASC 740 deferred-tax error (non-reliance), alongside cable-franchise impairments. Reasoning: Flags-judgment: here the flags (going-concern doubt, skipped coupon, restatement, a $4.1bn April-2027 maturity it cannot pay from cash) all point at the same event and have teeth. With a 'vast majority' ad hoc group already organised, the efficient route to bind holdouts across a ~$22bn multi-tranche structure is usually a pre-packaged or pre-negotiated Chapter 11; an out-of-court exchange is possible but needs near-unanimity. We lean above the reference class. Resolution: YES if Optimum Communications, Inc., CSC Holdings LLC or any parent/intermediate holding company of CSC Holdings files a voluntary or involuntary petition under Chapter 11 (including a pre-packaged case) on or before 30-Jun-2027, per an 8-K or the bankruptcy docket. A purely out-of-court exchange does not count. Source: SEC EDGAR 8-K filings of Optimum Communications (CIK 1702780) / PACER or claims-agent docket. Resolve by 2027-06-30; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: Reference class (unverified, from memory of rating-agency default studies): issuers that skip a coupon and enter a grace period while negotiating with an ad hoc group end in a bankruptcy filing within ~6–8 months a bit over half the time; the rest are distressed exchanges or extensions.

A purely out-of-court exchange does not count.
